test.title: A time when you changed your mind about something

document.cue: Describe a time when you changed your mind about something.

text: I'd like to talk about how I changed my mind about living in a dormitory. When I got a place at university in Almaty, I was offered a room in the student hostel, and my first reaction was to refuse, because I'd heard nothing but horror stories about noise, shared kitchens and cold showers.

My plan was to rent a small flat with my savings, even though it would have cost almost three times as much. I was sure that I needed my own space to study properly, and I told everyone who asked that the dormitory was out of the question.

What changed my mind was a conversation with my cousin, who had lived in the same hostel a few years earlier. She said that most of her closest friends today were people she met in the corridor there, and that she learned more English from her international neighbours than in class. Then she added, quite bluntly, that I'd be lonely in a flat on my own.

In the end I took the room, and she was absolutely right. The kitchen is noisy and the showers are sometimes cold, but I've made friends from four different countries, and we study together before exams. Looking back, my original decision was based on fear rather than facts.
Now I try to listen to people with real experience before making up my mind.

tips.en: Out of the question — the firmer the old view, the more interesting the change.
